route: route 1 (per-item published descriptives, split by group)
evidence: Paper Table 2 publishes mean+-SD per item separately for the experimental (peer-assisted, n=134) and control (faculty-led, n=63) groups plus a Mann-Whitney p; cov_group survives into the live table so all 24 means, 24 SDs and 12 p-values are recomputable. Every one matches: largest mean deviation 0.005, largest SD deviation 0.005 (B_8 control 0.89 obs vs 0.90 printed), e.g. B_6 4.10/3.17 obs vs 4.10/3.17 pub, B_7 3.16/2.77 vs 3.16/2.77, B_12 3.61/3.48 vs 3.61/3.48. The published (exp,ctl) mean pairs are distinct for all 12 items, so every item is separated from every other: B_3 and B_10 tie at exp 3.75 but split on control (3.33 vs 3.44), B_4 and B_8 tie at exp 3.99 but split on control (3.08 vs 3.23). The significance pattern also reproduces exactly, including that B_12 is the sole non-significant item (obs p=0.275 vs printed 0.274) -- the paper names that item by its wording ('the position and function of the retinacula of the wrist and the tendon sheaths of the wrist and hand'), independently pinning B_12. What this route does NOT establish: the option_text anchors (Not at all / A little bit / Somewhat / Quite a bit / Very much), which are taken from the questionnaire's own column headers printed directly over the codes 1-5 and need no inference.

route: 9 (response-frequency matching: raw survey file -> live integers) + 1 (per-item M/SD vs paper Table 2)
evidence: Raw survey file S1 (2,101 complete cases) vs live table (2,086 ids), response-level count vectors on the common 1-5 coding (live ISI01/ISI07 shifted +1). Diagonal L1 distance is 15 for all seven items -- exactly the 15-case sample difference -- against a best off-diagonal of 49, so the assignment source column k -> ISI0k is the unique best match by row and by column. Level counts, src vs live: src1 1159/604/202/95/41 vs ISI01 1151/599/202/93/41; src4 1123/507/246/144/81 vs ISI04 1115/502/245/143/81; src7 1339/492/190/51/29 vs ISI07 1332/485/189/51/29. The three closest rival pairs are still separated by 49-63. Independently, paper Table 2 per-item M (SD) reproduces to <=0.01 in order: 0.69(0.95)/1.57(0.90)/1.57(0.91)/1.84(1.12)/1.65(0.95)/1.61(0.90)/0.54(0.86) vs live 0.69(0.95)/1.57(0.91)/1.57(0.91)/1.84(1.12)/1.65(0.95)/1.61(0.90)/0.54(0.86). WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: the count match ties each live item to a source COLUMN, and for ISI04-ISI07 that column carries the question text in its own header, so those four are pinned outright; but ISI01-ISI03 are the three unlabelled components of one composite severity cell, so the route distinguishes them from each other and from the rest while saying nothing about which is falling asleep, staying asleep or early waking -- that ordering rests on the paper's labels and canonical ISI order. PARTIAL for that reason. It also cannot adjudicate the paper's Table 2 labels for ISI05-ISI07, which contradict the study's own script; the shipped text follows the script's by-name renames.
